newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: MANILA STOCKS FALL 1.05 PCT ON BLUE CHIPS SELLING.
newsitem.headline: MANILA STOCKS FALL 1.05 PCT ON BLUE CHIPS SELLING.

text.p: Philippine shares tumbled in early Tuesday trading from continued selling pressure in blue chip issues led by the Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co, traders said.
"Dearth of positive news, high interest rates, and volatility in Asian currency markets are pulling the market downwards," said Julie Villena, analyst at Magnum International Securities.
The main index fell 27.03 points, or 1.05 percent, to 2,545.40.
Dragging the index in early trade were firstliners PLDT, Manila Electric Co B, Petron Corp and San Miguel Corp B.

"PLDT is taking its toll on the market. For the rest of the session, we will be moving sideways. There's no positive news and there is still a lot of anxiety," said Jose Ricardo Garcia, executive vice-president at Diversified Securities.
Garcia said the market seemed to be indifferent to the news that international donors came to the rescue of Thailand with pledges of $16 billion in loans.
"People may be thinking that the bail-out of Thailand will take some time. They don't probably perceive the economy picking up," said Garcia.
